selection.reason: It has a real published narrative and a later contradictory trace; the other candidates lack a current discriminating event.

pre_result_plan.real_task: Independently review the factual claims in Agent 2's published day-3 journal before that narrative is reused as channel evidence.
pre_result_plan.observed_problem: The journal makes a completeness claim about owner requests, while a later repository audit found an older omitted intervention.
pre_result_plan.baseline: The published journal received no pre-review and records zero claim-level issues caught before publication.
pre_result_plan.hypothesis: A bounded evidence review will identify at least one contradicted or unsupported material claim without changing the other agent's text.
pre_result_plan.quality_control: Quote no private content; require direct repository traces for each finding; distinguish later evidence from what was visible at publication; keep supported claims and run the full suite.
pre_result_plan.overhead: Count startup reading, evidence inspection, report/docs/ledger/checkpoint work, tests and connector publication.
pre_result_plan.stop_condition: Review only the day-3 journal and directly relevant traces; make no site edit, schema extension or publisher feature. Report zero findings as inconclusive.

supported_material_claims.claim: The schedule request, resolved-conversation blocker and first scheduled site run were recorded.
Agent 1 found and repaired the omitted channel instruction.
The public, unreviewed site failed the channel publisher boundary twice.

findings.claim: The schedule intervention is in the public record 'like every other owner request.'
findings.evidence: Session 034 found that the 2026-09-30 GitHub Pages intervention had been absent for two days and repaired it.
findings.scope_note: The contradiction was documented after the day-3 journal was published. It invalidates reuse of the broad completeness wording now; it does not show that the author knowingly ignored available evidence at publication time.

result.reason: Keep claim-level evidence review as a manual pre-reuse step. One real catch does not justify changing the validator schema or editing another agent's published narrative in this session.
limitations: One journal entry and one contradicted claim; no broad accuracy or LLM-quality claim follows.
The decisive evidence appeared after publication, so this tests review before reuse, not prevention at initial publication.
The baseline and intervention are sequential rather than randomized, and elapsed time or token overhead was not measured comparably.
Catching the issue does not itself correct the already published site.
